MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In the fraction 7/10, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 17
   B. 7
   C. 3
   D. 10

2. What is 200 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 20
   C. 200
   D. 2

3. Which of these is a factor of 50? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 25
   C. 6
   D. 4

4. What is 79 ÷ 8? (1 mark)
   A. 9 remainder 7
   B. 10 remainder 7
   C. 8 remainder 15
   D. 9 remainder 8

5. A sweet costs 50 cents. How many sweets can you buy with Ksh 10? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 10
   C. 20
   D. 200

6. Which number is written in words as "three thousand, four hundred and fifty"? (1 mark)
   A. 3,450
   B. 345
   C. 3,540
   D. 34,500

7. One layer of a cuboid has 20 blocks and there are 4 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 24 blocks
   B. 80 blocks
   C. 100 blocks
   D. 76 blocks

8. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 12
   C. 11
   D. 10

9. What is 5 1/2 L − 3 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 1/2 L
   B. 2 3/4 L
   C. 2 L
   D. 2 1/4 L

10. A pencil starts at the 3 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 11 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 11 cm
   B. 8 cm
   C. 9 cm
   D. 14 cm

11. Which is greater, 0.6 or 0.06? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot be told
   B. 0.6
   C. They are equal
   D. 0.06

12. A big sponge is light but a small stone is heavy. What does this tell us? (1 mark)
   A. Size does not tell us the mass
   B. Mass is measured in metres
   C. Small things are always light
   D. Big things are always heavy

13. Njeri had Ksh 5,000 and bought a bag for Ksh 1,850. How much money does she have left? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 3,140
   B. Ksh 3,250
   C. Ksh 4,850
   D. Ksh 3,150

14. A hen lays 21 eggs in a month. How many eggs do 16 hens lay in a month? (1 mark)
   A. 336 eggs
   B. 326 eggs
   C. 436 eggs
   D. 316 eggs

15. Estimate 8,652 − 3,748 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 4,910
   B. 4,890
   C. 4,900
   D. 5,000

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. A rectangle has an area of 48 square units and 6 rows. How many columns does it have? Explain how you found out. (3 marks)

17. A triangle has two equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have? Explain how you can check. (3 marks)

18. Arrange 605, 560, 650 and 506 from smallest to largest. (3 marks)

19. Add 1 1/4 L and 2 1/2 L. Show your working. (3 marks)

20. A trader buys 18 crates with 35 bananas in each crate. How many bananas are there altogether? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 10
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

2. D — 2
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 200 ÷ 100 = 2.

3. B — 25
   50 ÷ 25 = 2 with nothing left over, so 25 is a factor of 50. The others leave a remainder.

4. A — 9 remainder 7
   8 × 9 = 72 and 79 − 72 = 7. So 79 ÷ 8 = 9 remainder 7. Check: 9 × 8 + 7 = 79.

5. C — 20
   Ksh 10 = 1,000 cents and 1,000 ÷ 50 = 20 sweets.

6. A — 3,450
   three thousand, four hundred and fifty: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 3,450.

7. B — 80 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 20 × 4 = 80 blocks.

8. D — 10
   Add all the numbers: 5 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 10.

9. D — 2 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 5 1/2 L − 3 1/4 L = 2 1/4 L.

10. B — 8 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 11 − 3 = 8 cm.

11. B — 0.6
   Compare the tenths first. 0.6 is greater than 0.06.

12. A — Size does not tell us the mass
   We must measure to know the mass. Size alone does not tell us.

13. D — Ksh 3,150
   Subtract 5,000 − 1,850 = 3,150. Check by adding: 3,150 + 1,850 = 5,000.

14. A — 336 eggs
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 336 eggs.

15. C — 4,900
   8,652 rounds to 8,650 and 3,748 rounds to 3,750. 8,650 − 3,750 = 4,900.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: 8 columns. Area = rows × columns, so columns = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the relationship, 1 mark for the division, 1 mark for 8.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: One line of symmetry. Fold it from the top corner to the middle of the base and the two halves match.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for one, 1 mark for the fold, 1 mark for the halves matching.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: 506, 560, 605, 650
   Working / marking points: Compare hundreds first, then tens. 1 mark for each correct pair of positions, up to 3 marks.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Wholes 1 + 2 = 3 (1 mark); parts 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4 (1 mark); total 3 3/4 L (1 mark).

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: 630 bananas
   Working / marking points: 18 × 5 = 90 (1 mark); 18 × 30 = 540 (1 mark); 90 + 540 = 630 (1 mark).
